subject: AtlasPay inference cost path & pilot framing
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: Samir Gupta <samir@atlaspay.com>, Elena Rodrigues <elena@atlaspay.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-17T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: AtlasPay inference cost path & pilot framing

Samir / Elena — thanks again for a productive demo earlier. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and the team can move the pilot paperwork along.

Call highlights (what we heard)
- Primary pain: inference spend variability during peak PSU reconciliation windows (mid-month spikes) causing degraded latency and unexpected costs.
- Workload: ~3M tokens/day today with growth to ~12M tokens/day in 6 months if feature ship goes ahead; majority are short completion calls (~20–80 tokens) plus periodic large batch reranks (300–800 tokens) for fraud detection pipelines.
- SLA targets: p95 latency <= 250ms for short calls; batch windows can accept 1–2s.
- Budget constraint: internal cap = $50k/month for initial pilot + production guardrails.

Cost levers we discussed
- Continuous batching for short calls (reduce per-token GPU overhead)
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts across reconciliation jobs (expected 25–40% token reduction for hot prefixes)
- Model selection + quantization profile (recommend A-Quantized v2 for balance of quality and cost)
- Routing policy: prioritize dedicated pool for peak windows with hosted fallback during overflow to bound costs.

Proposed pilot scope (2–4 weeks)
- Objectives: validate p95 latency <=250ms on production-ish traffic and demonstrate >=30% unit cost reduction vs current hosted baseline using batching + cache.
- Deliverables: run two 72-hour runs (normal and peak-sim) with token-level billing and latency traces; redwood provides TokenEcon_Snapshot and ops runbook.
- Success criteria: average unit cost <= $0.00095/token on normal run and peak p95 <=250ms.

Next steps (owners & timing)
- AtlasPay: share a 7-day sample of production traffic and any existing cacheable prompt lists (Samir) — due Wed 4/20.
- Redwood: deliver a scoped pilot SOW and token econ model (Lauren) — draft to you by Fri 4/21.
- Procurement: if pilot OK, we’ll send a short PO template and MOU for signature to enable Dedicated capacity provisioning (Marissa will own).

Attachments: AtlasPay_TokenEcon_Snapshot.xlsx (draft cost model), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Open questions we flagged
- Is AtlasPay willing to isolate peak windows onto a small Dedicated pool for the pilot, or must we keep everything on hosted? (routing affects pricing model)
- Any compliance constraints on log retention beyond standard 30-day traces?

If that matches your readout I’ll send the pilot SOW and a short MOU. Otherwise tell me what I missed.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0197

Attachments: AtlasPay_TokenEcon_Snapshot.xlsx, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

From: Samir Gupta <samir@atlaspay.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Rodrigues <elena@atlaspay.com>, ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-17T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasPay inference cost path & pilot framing

Thanks Lauren — very clear and helpful. Quick clarifications from our side:
- We can provide the 7-day sample by EOD Wed. I’ll scrub PII, but keep request IDs and timing.
- Peak windows: we’d prefer to avoid Dedicated for now unless there’s a firm cost predictability guarantee. That said, we’re open to a hybrid for the pilot if you can show the delta in the SOW.
- Budget: the $50k/month cap is soft for the pilot if the ROI is locked to measurable fraud-reduction or reduced manual reconciliation hours. We need a business-case template you can populate (tokens -> ops hours saved).

Also Elena will loop in procurement for PO template — Elena, looping you so procurement knows timeline.

Samir
Head of Payments Engineering — AtlasPay
samir@atlaspay.com

On 2028-04-17 15:22, lauren.bishop@redwood.com wrote:
> Samir / Elena — thanks again for a productive demo earlier. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and the team can move the pilot paperwork along.

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-18T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: AtlasPay pilot guardrails / pricing note

Lauren — short internal note to lock the ask before I draft numbers:
- If they want no Dedicated commitment, we should price a capped-hosted pilot with a per-token blended rate and a hard spend cap ($50k) + overage approval. That preserves their constraint but still covers our peak infra cost.
- If they accept a small Dedicated pool for peak windows (e.g., 2x V100-equivalent), we can give a 20–25% unit-cost improvement at the pilot level.
- I’ll prepare two pricing options: (A) Hosted-capped pilot; (B) Hybrid Dedicated for peak + hosted fallback. Need your SOW language for deliverables to align acceptance criteria.

Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: none

From: Elena Rodrigues <elena@atlaspay.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@atlaspay.com
Date: 2028-04-18T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasPay inference cost path & pilot framing — procurement note

Thanks — confirms our internal view. Procurement expects a one-page PO + SOW. A couple of items to call out so our team can review quickly:
- Data handling: we can accept 30-day traces; anything beyond requires a written attestation and a security contact at Redwood.
- Invoicing cadence: prefer a single pilot invoice at completion with itemized token breakdowns.
- Liability: standard limits are fine, but we’ll need SOC2 summary and the SLAs in SOW for latency.

I’ve attached a light PO template (AtlasPay_PO_Request.docx) and included procurement on cc for timeline. Samir — we’ll aim to send the sample traffic by Wed.

Elena
VP, Operations — AtlasPay
elena@atlaspay.com
